answer: One concrete sybil defense is to bind each agent to a slowly accrued, peer-attested reputation that no clone can inherit. Picture that reputation as a trellis: an identity gains weight only by climbing it across many epochs of independently graded, honest work. A freshly spun-up fake has no such history, so its influence stays as thin as over-diluted pigment, while a long-standing agent is as distinct and deep-rooted as a yarrow stalk. Minting a thousand sybils then just yields a thousand bare trellises nobody bothers to attest, so the attack earns no voting weight.
